minimum_next_source_contract.kind: Additive original MinIO bootstrap authority, reviewed with A/C/D. This is a proposed contract, not an implemented or installed schema.
minimum_next_source_contract.registration: Existing enrolled operator and original owner key must install an explicit MinIO purpose-domain authority BEFORE bootstrap in the exact original database/account/server namespace. It must be independent of future active config/task rows. Reuse original identity authentication, not the capture record's resource authorization.
minimum_next_source_contract.sql_source: Define separately typed original MinIO permission head/grant/ref rows (or another already existing controlled authoritative SQL source after evidence is supplied). Current capture-domain rows cannot be repurposed. D owns migration/installation mechanics; no ad-hoc CREATE/INSERT executed or added to bootstrap checks here.

namespace/provider deployment and resource immutable identities
original minio permission profile + epoch/head state/current row version
domain-separated signed grant/head raw bytes/hash/signature + original public pin and absolute windows

minimum_next_source_contract.write_and_revoke_rules: Owner installer creates initial rows only after authenticating original enrollment/admin and actual native observation. Atomic CAS governs original head/ref epoch and revocation with a documented lock order. Consumer uses that actual source, not a SQL cache lacking controlled revocation. Kubernetes and SQL dual-source drift must fail closed, with explicit partial/unknown-commit recovery; no implicit self-enrollment or overwrite.
minimum_next_source_contract.prepare: Separate per-purpose BootstrapResourceValidator constructs privately owned one-shot state. Decode exact BootstrapConfig/OfflineBootstrapGrant and match all five references and original config hash. Read installed MinIO grant/head and original current SQL source outside consumer locks; perform concrete native permission and independent capability observations with readback/tails; snapshot immutable descriptors and actual fixed credential identities. Do not construct DeploymentService or require an already-active publication config.
minimum_next_source_contract.l2: After the existing original admin/RBAC prefix and BEFORE operation/history lookup, AuthorizeBootstrapOriginal uses the SAME supplied tx (candidate path: controlled pd.BootstrapSQL) to sample SQL time and read/lock current original MinIO head/grant/ref rows in reviewed order. Compare exact signed original identities, purpose/ref mappings, epoch/state/row versions and windows to Prepare; retain guard bound to same context/transaction/config/grant. No network, provider calls, credential hashing, new preparation or Commit/Rollback.
minimum_next_source_contract.freshness: Explicit finite native-observation deadline must be distinct from long owner grant/credential validity, clipped to all original windows and an independently reviewed profile maximum. Capture the observation start/end; do not issue a renewed observation deadline in L2 or tail. Current v2 source Until alone must not be treated as this short lease.
minimum_next_source_contract.fresh_use_tail: Actual external permission/capability tail measurements belong to lock-free Prepare. At fresh-use Work-end Recheck, repeat original SQL identity/window/ref mapping through the same controlled transaction and check the private immutable native observation is still within its fixed short deadline, plus allowed local pin/resource checks. No provider I/O in Recheck. If a requirement demands a new network sample after locking, the attempt must release/rollback and perform a new outside-lock preparation under a separately reviewed orchestration; it cannot smuggle network I/O into the callback.
minimum_next_source_contract.history: Keep original L2 current identity/ref authority for exact historical retries. Missing/expired physical observation refuses fresh consumption; do not require a new capability probe before the operation/history branch just to return authorized exact history. Candidate adapter must separately carry identity and dependency deadlines and preserve replay semantics.
minimum_next_source_contract.capability_probe: Use an independently owner-authorized finite probe intent with exact keys/versions/checksums, role credentials, bounded bytes and original cleanup/retention ownership; no future task IDs/config-derived admission, arbitrary probes, production-object deletion, or widening existing role policy. Probe mutations and any retained immutable catalog probe must be explicitly inventoried and reviewed before execution. Existing permission-only observation is not this source.
minimum_next_source_contract.d_link: Once genuine sources/probes exist, add five concrete adapters in independent files, compose them into BootstrapOwnerAdapters.References via a reviewed compiled function and layer the same concrete owner into CandidateAuthority sessions. D then explicitly invokes the composition from the real main bootstrap entry. Requirements output must still list every unrelated missing owner. Do not alter disaster qualification or isolated-restore prerequisites for ordinary functional backup publication.

anti_cycle_rules: Do not call DeploymentService.CheckCurrentEffectiveV2 or CheckPublicationDependenciesWithMinIOEffectiveV2 from first-install Prepare: these reopen active publication config/Forward/runtime/SQL sources that bootstrap is creating.

Use original independently pinned disabled bootstrap config/grant plus pre-existing owner authority and current native resources instead. The existing taskless producer observer is the concrete non-active-config starting point.

Do not generate initial ref identity from credential secret bytes, fabricate registered refs, derive issuer pin from the signed candidate, or treat a current policy response's hash as its own original trust authority.

Do not implement an allow-all Original, callback-provided Passed, identity-only MinIO validator, generic capture signer substitution, or a non-authorizing metadata matcher disguised as BootstrapResourceValidator.
